payload.reasoning: Exhaustive screen of every testable factor in the federated mesh.

hypotheses.title: Firmware overcharge bug
hypotheses.claim: A BMS firmware release overcharges cells
hypotheses.rationale: Customers mention recent firmware updates (v3.2 and v3.4) in posts.
hypotheses.verdict: Ruled out. Failure rate is flat across firmware (5.7/10k to 7.6/10k, p = 0.44).

hypotheses.title: Carrier transit shock
hypotheses.claim: Rough handling by one carrier damages packs in transit
hypotheses.rationale: A customer blames UPS shipping damage for swelling.
hypotheses.verdict: Ruled out. Failure rate is flat across carrier (5.6/10k to 7.7/10k, p = 0.33).

hypotheses.title: Sun Belt heat exposure
hypotheses.claim: High ambient heat in Sun Belt markets drives thermal events
hypotheses.rationale: Cluster is concentrated in Phoenix and Austin; one post blames 101F heat.
hypotheses.verdict: Ruled out as a confounder. SUNBELT only looks guilty because it shares units with CB-B-0917; holding cell_batch fixed, the effect disappears (p = 0.23).

hypotheses.title: Plant assembly defect
hypotheses.claim: One assembly plant has a process defect
hypotheses.rationale: Packs differ by assembly plant; plant processes affect weld quality.
hypotheses.verdict: Ruled out as a confounder. P2 only looks guilty because it shares units with CB-B-0917; holding cell_batch fixed, the effect disappears (p = 0.27).

hypotheses.title: BMS board supplier
hypotheses.claim: A battery-management board supplier ships faulty boards
hypotheses.rationale: Overcharge can come from the battery-management board, not firmware.
hypotheses.verdict: Ruled out as a confounder. BMS-Orion only looks guilty because it shares units with CB-B-0917; holding cell_batch fixed, the effect disappears (p = 0.97).

hypotheses.title: Cell supplier quality
hypotheses.claim: One cell supplier has systemic quality problems
hypotheses.verdict: Ruled out as a confounder. Supplier B only looks guilty because it shares units with CB-B-0917; holding cell_batch fixed, the effect disappears (p = 0.27).

hypotheses.title: Defective cell batch
hypotheses.claim: A specific incoming cell batch is defective
hypotheses.rationale: Several posts say the pack is "from early October", hinting at a production window.
hypotheses.verdict: Confirmed. CB-B-0917 fails at 841/10k vs 0.5/10k elsewhere (RR 1668x, 95% CI 848-3280). It holds up after adjusting for every other factor and accounts for 93% of incidents.

evidence.label: Red-team review
evidence.summary: 6/6 objections answered by evidence

objections.objection: Hot climates could be cooking these packs instead.
objections.result: CB-B-0917 still significant controlling for H-HEAT (p < 1e-300), H-PLANT (p < 1e-300), H-BMS (p < 1e-300), H-SUPPLIER (p < 1e-300)

objections.objection: Some regions may simply complain more, inflating claims.
objections.result: Within each warehouse CB-B-0917 still fails far more often (CMH p < 1e-300). Regional reporting habits cannot explain it.

objections.objection: Older units fail more; maybe these units have just been in use longer.
objections.result: CB-B-0917 units: 15.9 days in field on average vs 45.1 for others. Less exposure yet more failures, so wear-out bias works against the finding.

objections.objection: With this many groups tested, one will look bad by chance.
objections.result: CB-B-0917: p < 1e-300 after testing 7 hypotheses; Bonferroni alpha 1.4e-3

objections.objection: Maybe the problem is broader and we are about to under-recall.
objections.result: Other batches from the same supplier fail at baseline (p = 0.24). The defect is specific to CB-B-0917.

objections.objection: An average can hide subgroups where the effect reverses.
objections.result: CB-B-0917: firmware consistent, carrier consistent, climate_zone consistent, bms_supplier consistent, warehouse_id consistent

evidence.label: Explanation
evidence.summary: 10/10 figures verified against evidence
evidence.payload:
Traceon traced 116 thermal incidents on the VR-48 pack to Defective cell batch: Supplier B CB-B-0917 (116 incidents, 1668x the baseline rate; L-409 (plant P2, built 2026-10-02 to 2026-10-04, serials SN-88400 to SN-89779)). Together they account for 92.8% of all thermal claims.

Firmware overcharge bug, Carrier transit shock showed no association at all. Sun Belt heat exposure, Plant assembly defect, BMS board supplier, Cell supplier quality looked guilty on raw numbers only because they share units with the real cause; holding the cause fixed, the effect vanishes.

Each confirmed cause survives adjustment for every other factor, holds across firmware, carrier, climate and warehouse subgroups, and has a consistent failure signature.

Recommended action: surgical quarantine for 1,380 units, instead of recalling 180,000, saving $4,465,500. Without action, a constant-hazard projection gives about 200 more incidents in 30 days. This was detectable on 2026-10-10, after 3 claims.
